public_rationale: The February 3, 2026 International AI Safety Report describes continuing failures, including fabricated information, flawed code, and misleading advice. It says current techniques cannot reduce failure rates to the level required in many high-stakes settings and that autonomous agents make timely human intervention harder [e1]. Within the February 1–25 assessment window, this supports the contextual claim that generative AI is insufficiently reliable for consequential decisions without human verification [e1].
limitations: The report does not establish that every generative model is unreliable for every task or that supervised applications cannot be useful [e1].
The report does not validate a particular military deployment against a specified acceptable error rate [e1].

our_interpretation: In context, the ordinary reading concerns depending on generative AI to avoid serious errors in consequential decisions without human verification.
It does not mean that every output is wrong or that no supervised application is useful.
Use February 1–25, 2026 as the latest pre-post assessment window for the ongoing state of the technology; the speaker supplies no reporting period.
criteria.support_condition: Relevant evaluations or a credible synthesis establish persistent material errors and insufficient reliability for consequential autonomous use.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative validation establishes dependable performance across the consequential autonomous uses described, with serious errors controlled to applicable safety requirements.
